runs.name: Public Service Enterprise Group Incorporated; NYSE PEG, SEC CIK 0000788784, New Jersey, 10-K filer jointly with PSE&G; public utility holding company: PSE&G, FERC-regulated transmission and BPU-regulated electric and gas distribution to about 2.4 million electric and 1.9 million gas customers in New Jersey, and PSEG Power, merchant nuclear in PJM; PSEG Long Island operates LIPA's system under contract; no rename, merger, spin-off or split in the 8-Ks since June 2025; $500M 4.800% senior notes 2026-06-03; the 10-K names no rival, Exelon, FirstEnergy and Constellation chosen as a CONVENTION of the run
runs.file: 2026-10-26 Run - PEG Public Service Enterprise Group.md
runs.entry: The v5 re-run order, unattended work-hours cycle, one dispatched analyst under the canonical brief; the brief's departures: the repository path after the move of 2026-10-25, the lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7, and the rivals taken from the 10-K. Price **$72.18** (2026-10-26, aggregator, flagged) x **498,420,030 shares** (10-Q cover at 2026-07-20, `0001193125-26-332943`; agreed with issued less treasury; PSE&G's 132,450,344 shares, all held by PEG, not added) = cap **$35,976M**; sovereign **5.33%** (Treasury 30-year, 2026-10-23). Read from the 10-K FY2025 (`0001193125-26-077446`), the 10-Ks FY2023 and FY2021, the 10-Q for 2026-06-30, the DEF 14A of 2026-03-12 and the earnings 8-Ks of 2026-02-26 and 2026-08-04; cross-checked figure operating cash 2025 $3,298M. **Q1 IN** on PSE&G, the deciding part (five-year operating income $10,377M against Power & Other -$834M); BPU 9.6% on 55% equity, FERC 9.90% plus a 0.5% adder. **Q2 IN** on the franchise (74% of New Jersey's population), the regulated return carried to Q3 as a second best; threats named: affordability politics after PJM capacity prices rose about tenfold, FERC Order 1000 competition; Power a price-taker in PJM, not deciding. **Q3 weighs against** (added capital about 6.4% pre-tax). **Q4 no STOP, weighs against** (non-GAAP Operating Earnings featured and guided, a 21-year streak at or above guidance; no restatement or material weakness; ten balance sheets 2016 to 2025, long-term debt $10.9B to $21.7B against equity $13.1B to $17.0B, dividends of $5.7B against $6.8B of net income over five years). **Q5 OUT on integrity, on doubt [M2013-088]**: a FERC civil penalty of $6.6M with compliance requirements (December 2024, Roseland-Pleasant Valley transmission project) for a violation the 10-K does not describe; two law-firm summaries (secondary sources, flagged; the FERC order in Docket IN21-5-000 not read, the fetch refused) describe it as incomplete information given to PJM in seeking the project's approval; read with the guidance streak on the figure incentive pay is set on; a BPU management audit's recommendations still undetermined. The analyst first committed Q5 as IN narrowly (`6f37af05`), then found the FERC matter in the 10-K and corrected it to OUT before Q6 was written (`1bc49585`), declared in the run file; the analyst notes a reader could argue TOO HARD (WORK). Q6 to Q12 not reached. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash after all spending -$653M a year 2021 to 2025; no-growth stream equity-only $1,480M a year (PSE&G after maintenance $1,273M with D&A as the proxy, Power & Other $239M, stock pay -$32M); growth cut to sales growth under (f) then capped at 5.33%; growth spending $2,247M in year one to $3,586M in year ten; utility debt credit $1,230M a year at a 57.65% cap (PEG's own long-term debt share; the BPU's 45% applies to the distribution base only, under half of the rate base; with the 45% cap the range is $55.73 to $57.73 and fair $26.00); range **$55.73 to $63.14 a share equity-only (central, regulated utility)**; 4.1% at the price; fair price **$28.15 equity-only**, all-equity range $8.36 to $25.63 and fair -$20.50, not positive; no case earns the floor. Peers (the 10-K names none; a CONVENTION of the run): return on equity 2021 to 2025 PSE&G 9.5%, Exelon 8.0%, FirstEnergy 9.3%, Constellation 15.7% (2022 to 2025, for Power). Framework gaps for the operator: the utility debt-credit cap where the allowed share covers only part of the rate base and whether the business is the holding company or the subsidiary; specific (f)'s sales growth including pass-through commodity costs; Q5 names no box for its STOP and no rule for an integrity fact whose primary document is knowable but unread; Q6's buyback line in a file closed at Q5. Could not get: the FERC order, the BPU audit findings, historical prices for the retention test, run.py's owner-earnings table (stopped at 2024, no depreciation; not used). Dispatcher's check: check_framework PASS; pathspec commits, own paths only (last `2641c3cc`); 54 ids resolve, no E-ids, no citation slip, 39 adjacent fragment pairs checked (`dispatcher_cite_check.py`), two pairings the script attached to the preceding id resolved by hand against their own rows (M2000-037, L2009-012); no tracked research file over 200 KB. Contamination declared: session-start commit subjects of the PPL run and a research folder name; none used. Position note filled at the fold: not held. Not armed: the box is not OUT at Q7 or IN.
runs.narr: OUT at Q5 on integrity, on doubt: a New Jersey regulated franchise whose castle stands, closed by a $6.6M FERC civil penalty over a transmission project the 10-K does not explain (secondary sources: incomplete information given to PJM), read with a 21-year guidance streak on the non-GAAP figure pay is set on; re-look condition the FERC order and the BPU audit. Computation only: equity-only range $55.73 to $63.14 vs $72.18, fair $28.15 equity-only, no case earns the floor.
